articles.title: At SCO summit In Kyrgyzstan, Guterres calls for more representative global governance
articles.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres on Tuesday urged leaders of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) to help reshape global governance for a changing world, arguing that a more multipolar international order can strengthen multilateralism, advance fairness and better serve developing countries.
articles.content:
Addressing the SCO summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, the Secretary-General said shifting global power dynamics present an opportunity to build more representative international institutions and a United Nations that works "at the service of all without double standards in line with the Charter."

The Shanghai Cooperation Organization is a Eurasian political, economic and security grouping founded in 2001 that today brings together 10 member States, including China, India, Pakistan, Russia and several Central Asian countries. It is one of the world's largest regional organizations by population and geographic scope.

‘A good thing’

“Our world is increasingly multipolar,” Mr. Guterres said. “That is a good thing and must be strengthened.”

He described multipolarity as “a condition for justice in global governance and international relations” and “the best support for effective multilateralism.”

The UN chief noted that while global power relations have evolved significantly, many international institutions continue to reflect the geopolitical realities of 1945.

“We must reform our multilateral institutions, including the United Nations and the Bretton Woods system, to reflect today's realities, and increase the representation and influence of developing countries to build a just world order,” he said.

He also praised the longstanding partnership between the UN and the SCO, describing the organization as “an important pillar of multilateralism.”

Four priorities for deeper cooperation

The Secretary-General outlined four areas where he believes cooperation between the UN and SCO can be strengthened.

1. Global security

Mr. Guterres voiced concern over continuing instability in the Middle East, warning that ceasefires and agreements are repeatedly being violated.

“I appeal for maximum restraint and for agreements and international law to be respected,” he said.

He stressed the need for “a peaceful, just and durable settlement” that would restore regional stability while safeguarding international navigational rights and freedoms, including around the Straits of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab.

Turning to Gaza, the Secretary-General said the ceasefire “must be respected” and called for the full implementation of the Comprehensive Plan to End the Gaza Conflict.

He also demanded the removal of obstacles hindering humanitarian assistance and renewed his call for an end to settler attacks and settlement expansion in the occupied West Bank.

“There will only be peace with a two-State solution,” he said, envisioning Israel and Palestine as “two independent, sovereign, democratic states” living side by side in peace and security, with Jerusalem/Al Quds serving as the capital of both.

On Ukraine, Mr. Guterres said that after more than four years of war, “it is high time for a full and immediate ceasefire.”

Such a step, he added, would open the way to negotiations towards “a just, lasting and comprehensive peace in line with international law.”

2. Financing for development

The Secretary-General called for reforms to the international financial system, arguing that developing countries continue to be burdened by unsustainable debt.

“We must reform the global financial architecture to introduce justice and equity and seriously address the debt that is strangling so many developing countries,” he said.

He also urged multilateral development banks to become “bigger, better and bolder” in supporting countries' development efforts.

3. Climate action

Warning that the world is on track to exceed the 1.5°C temperature limit, the UN chief called for rapid emissions cuts and a faster transition to renewable energy.

“Climate action requires climate justice,” he said, underscoring the need for substantially greater financial support for developing countries.

He also highlighted the importance of managing critical minerals responsibly and ensuring producing countries receive greater benefits from their natural resources.

“No more plundering,” he said.

4. Artificial intelligence

The Secretary-General said artificial intelligence must work for all countries, not just a few.

That, he stressed, will require effective guardrails and more inclusive governance mechanisms.

Meeting with Iranian President

On the margins of the summit, the Secretary-General also met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian.

According to a UN spokesperson, during the meeting, Mr. Guterres expressed concern over the devastating humanitarian and economic consequences of the conflict in Iran, across the region and beyond.

He stressed the urgent need to resolve the crisis through dialogue and negotiations, with full respect for international law, including international navigational rights and freedoms in and around the Strait of Hormuz.

The Secretary-General also reaffirmed the United Nations commitment to support diplomatic efforts aimed at achieving a comprehensive and durable solution.

articles.personality_title: UN chief urges fairer global leadership at SCO summit
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – The Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) is a group of 10 countries from Eurasia, including China, India, Russia, and others. It focuses on political, economic, and security cooperation. The United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres spoke at their summit in Kyrgyzstan to discuss changes needed in global leadership.

**What happened** – On June 27, 2023, Mr. Guterres called on SCO leaders to help reshape global governance. He said the world is becoming multipolar, meaning power is shared among many countries instead of just a few. He wants international institutions like the UN to better reflect today’s realities and give more voice to developing countries. He outlined four key areas for cooperation: global security, fair financing, climate action, and fair rules for artificial intelligence (AI).

**Impact** – This call is important because it recognizes that many international organizations still work based on old power structures from after World War II. By making these institutions more fair and representative, developing countries can have a stronger say in decisions that affect them. For example, Mr. Guterres stressed the need for peace in conflict areas like Gaza, Ukraine, and the Middle East, better financial support for poorer countries, faster action on climate change, and fair use of AI technology worldwide.

**What's next step** – The SCO and UN will likely work more closely on these priorities. Changes to global financial systems and international institutions could begin, and new agreements on security and climate might be pursued. The UN will also keep encouraging dialogue to resolve conflicts and support sustainable development.

**One-sentence takeaway** – The UN Secretary-General’s message at the SCO summit highlights the need for a fairer world where more countries share power and work together on peace, finance, climate, and technology.
articles.personality_title_fr: Le chef de l’ONU appelle à un leadership mondial plus juste lors du sommet de l’OCS
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – L’Organisation de coopération de Shanghai (OCS) regroupe 10 pays d’Eurasie, dont la Chine, l’Inde et la Russie. Elle se concentre sur la coopération politique, économique et sécuritaire. Le Secrétaire général de l’ONU, António Guterres, a pris la parole lors de leur sommet au Kirghizistan pour parler des changements nécessaires dans la gouvernance mondiale.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Le 27 juin 2023, M. Guterres a demandé aux dirigeants de l’OCS d’aider à remodeler la gouvernance mondiale. Il a expliqué que le monde devient multipolaire, c’est-à-dire que le pouvoir est partagé entre plusieurs pays au lieu de quelques-uns seulement. Il souhaite que les institutions internationales comme l’ONU reflètent mieux la réalité d’aujourd’hui et donnent plus de voix aux pays en développement. Il a présenté quatre domaines clés de coopération : la sécurité mondiale, un financement équitable, l’action climatique et des règles justes pour l’intelligence artificielle (IA).

**Impact** – Cet appel est important car il reconnaît que beaucoup d’organisations internationales fonctionnent encore selon d’anciens rapports de force datant de la Seconde Guerre mondiale. En rendant ces institutions plus justes et représentatives, les pays en développement pourront mieux participer aux décisions qui les concernent. Par exemple, M. Guterres a souligné le besoin de paix dans des zones de conflit comme Gaza, l’Ukraine et le Moyen-Orient, un meilleur soutien financier aux pays pauvres, une action plus rapide contre le changement climatique et une utilisation équitable de la technologie IA dans le monde.

**Prochaine étape** – L’OCS et l’ONU vont probablement renforcer leur collaboration sur ces priorités. Des changements dans les systèmes financiers mondiaux et les institutions internationales pourraient commencer, et de nouveaux accords sur la sécurité et le climat pourraient être recherchés. L’ONU continuera aussi à encourager le dialogue pour résoudre les conflits et soutenir le développement durable.

**Message clé en une phrase** – Le message du Secrétaire général de l’ONU au sommet de l’OCS souligne la nécessité d’un monde plus juste où davantage de pays partagent le pouvoir et travaillent ensemble pour la paix, la finance, le climat et la technologie.
articles.personality_title_es: El jefe de la ONU pide un liderazgo mundial más justo en la cumbre de la OCS
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – La Organización de Cooperación de Shanghái (OCS) es un grupo de 10 países de Eurasia, incluyendo China, India y Rusia. Se centra en la cooperación política, económica y de seguridad. El Secretario General de la ONU, António Guterres, habló en su cumbre en Kirguistán para discutir cambios necesarios en el liderazgo mundial.

**Qué pasó** – El 27 de junio de 2023, Guterres pidió a los líderes de la OCS que ayuden a reformar la gobernanza global. Dijo que el mundo se está volviendo multipolar, es decir, el poder se comparte entre muchos países en lugar de solo unos pocos. Quiere que las instituciones internacionales como la ONU reflejen mejor la realidad actual y den más voz a los países en desarrollo. Señaló cuatro áreas clave para cooperar: seguridad global, financiamiento justo, acción climática y reglas justas para la inteligencia artificial (IA).

**Impacto** – Esta llamada es importante porque reconoce que muchas organizaciones internacionales aún funcionan según estructuras de poder antiguas de después de la Segunda Guerra Mundial. Al hacer estas instituciones más justas y representativas, los países en desarrollo pueden tener una voz más fuerte en las decisiones que les afectan. Por ejemplo, Guterres destacó la necesidad de paz en zonas de conflicto como Gaza, Ucrania y Medio Oriente, mejor apoyo financiero para países pobres, acción más rápida sobre el clima y uso justo de la tecnología IA en todo el mundo.

**Próximo paso** – La OCS y la ONU probablemente trabajarán más cerca en estas prioridades. Podrían comenzar cambios en los sistemas financieros globales y las instituciones internacionales, y buscar nuevos acuerdos sobre seguridad y clima. La ONU también seguirá promoviendo el diálogo para resolver conflictos y apoyar el desarrollo sostenible.

**Mensaje en una frase** – El mensaje del Secretario General de la ONU en la cumbre de la OCS destaca la necesidad de un mundo más justo donde más países compartan el poder y trabajen juntos por la paz, las finanzas, el clima y la tecnología.
